text:
jess: Customer (acme-123) reporting monthly credits dropped to 0 while a long-running streaming job was active, ~6h before their expected refill. They got a bunch of 429s and stream aborted. Posting logs and session info.

jess: session_id=stream-7f3a, start=2026-03-12T03:10:00Z, region=us-west-2, org=acme-123

jess: logs:
```
[2026-03-12T09:58:30Z] req=abc123 org=acme-123 tokens_used=4800 remaining=0
[2026-03-12T10:02:45Z] req=abc124 org=acme-123 response=429 quota_exhausted
[2026-03-12T15:58:45Z] billing_event=promo_topup org=acme-123 amount=10000 status=received
[2026-03-12T16:00:03Z] billing_event=apply_topup org=acme-123 status=applied new_balance=10000
```

samir: thanks — can you confirm the customer timezone and whether they performed a manual top-up? also any client reconnects during that window?

jess: customer on PST, they did a promo top-up around 15:58 UTC (08:58 PST). No reconnects on their side, stream stayed alive the whole time.

olivia: likely timeline: platform billing job runs at 16:00 UTC for that billing window; promo events are queued then applied. UI and some services use cached usage/remaining values for a short TTL; long-lived streams may not re-check an org balance until they attempt allocation. So customer saw 0 until the apply job finished and until a new allocation/check occurred.

billing-eng: confirmed: the top-up event arrived and was processed, but the apply job batch runs at 16:00 UTC. The apply completed at 16:00:03Z. The streaming allocator only queries latest balance on new token allocations, not continuously for open sessions.

jess: customer upset because their demo cut off before their scheduled refill. They want a reproducible explanation and mitigation.

samir: short-term mitigation: ask customer to reconnect stream after refill or perform an explicit balance check call (e.g., GET /v1/orgs/acme-123/usage) once they expect the top-up. For long-running streams, recommend a small client-side reconnect/heartbeat that triggers a balance refresh after the known reset time.

olivia: long-term: we should consider adding a hook so billing apply events push a cache invalidation to streaming allocators or the stream runtime subscribes to balance-change events. Filing a follow-up for infra.

billing-eng: created internal task: BILL-4982 to push cache-invalidations on apply. Also note: promo top-ups that occur within a minute of the batch may appear to the customer as "late" by a few seconds — that's expected. We'll document this behavior.

support-bot: Created ticket INC-8621 and linked to BILL-4982. :white_check_mark:

jess: will share this thread with the customer and propose two options: 1) reconnect right after reset, 2) schedule top-ups earlier than expected reset to avoid edge race. Also offer 1-hour courtesy credit while we improve infra.

samir: please include repro steps for eng: 1) create org with low balance, 2) start long streaming session in us-west-2, 3) trigger promo top-up within 2 minutes before apply batch, 4) observe 429s until apply job completes and client reconnect absent. Add logs above.

olivia: adding note: timezone confusion often stems from customers expecting local-midnight resets; our monthly-billing job runs at the account's configured cycle UTC anchor (documented). We'll update docs to call this out more clearly and add FAQ.

jess: thanks all — I'll draft a response to the customer with logs and mitigation steps. Marking as pending follow-up until BILL-4982 and INC-8621 resolved. :thumbsup:
